recommendations.text: High-quality CPR with a compression rate of 100-120/min, depth of 5-6 cm, full recoil, and minimal interruptions is the foundation of resuscitation.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Cardiac Arrest Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - confirm cardiac arrest (within 1 minutes) - activate code team (within 2 minutes) - begin high quality cpr (within 1 minutes) - attach defibrillator pads (within 3 minutes)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Cardiac Arrest Initial Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay cpr, delay defibrillation, interrupt cpr for intubation extended.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: After initial CPR, check rhythm. If VF/pVT, proceed to defibrillation. If asystole/PEA, continue CPR and administer epinephrine.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Rhythm Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - analyze rhythm (within 2 minutes)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Rhythm Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay cpr, interrupt cpr prolonged.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For VF/pVT, defibrillate as soon as possible. Epinephrine should be given after the second shock. Amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered for shock-refractory VF/pVT.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Shockable Rhythm Pathway (VF/pVT), the following actions are mandatory: - deliver defibrillation (within 2 minutes) - resume cpr immediately (within 2 minutes) - give epinephrine 1mg iv (within 10 minutes) - give amiodarone 300mg (within 10 minutes)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Shockable Rhythm Pathway (VF/pVT), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay cpr, delay defibrillation.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: atropine removed from cardiac arrest algorithm post-2010 ACLS update; no evidence of benefit in VF/pVT [FORBIDDEN: give_atropine_for_cardiac_arrest] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 5.1; AHA removed atropine from ACLS algorithm in 2010

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: calcium is not routinely indicated in cardiac arrest unless hyperkalemia (K>6.5) or calcium channel blocker toxicity is present [FORBIDDEN: give_calcium_without_indication] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 6.2; calcium indicated only for hyperkalemia or calcium channel blocker toxicity

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: routine bicarbonate not recommended unless severe acidosis (pH <7.1) or known hyperkalemia [FORBIDDEN: give_sodium_bicarbonate_routine] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 6.2; bicarbonate only for severe acidosis (pH <7.1) or hyperkalemia

recommendations.text: In shockable rhythms, defibrillation takes priority over drug administration; epinephrine given after 2nd shock. [BEFORE: deliver_defibrillation, give_epinephrine_1mg_iv] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 5.1; Kudenchuk PJ, NEJM 2016

recommendations.text: In shockable rhythm, defibrillation takes absolute priority; amiodarone before first shock and intubation delays worsen outcomes. [FORBIDDEN: give_amiodarone_before_first_shock, delay_defibrillation_for_intubation] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; defibrillation is the definitive treatment for VF/pVT; each minute delay reduces survival by 7-10%

recommendations.text: Hyperkalemia is a reversible cause of cardiac arrest; calcium chloride stabilizes myocardium, bicarbonate and insulin shift potassium intracellularly. [REQUIRED: give_calcium_chloride, give_sodium_bicarbonate, give_insulin_dextrose] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.2: Reversible Causes; Montague BT, Resuscitation 2008

recommendations.text: Succinylcholine worsens hyperkalemia via K+ release from muscle; calcium gluconate delay prolongs fatal cardiac toxicity. [FORBIDDEN: give_succinylcholine_in_hyperkalemic_arrest, delay_calcium_in_hyperkalemic_arrest] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; succinylcholine releases K+ from muscle; calcium delay prolongs cardiac toxicity window

recommendations.text: Below 30C, cardiac drugs are ineffective and may accumulate to toxic levels; focus on rewarming and CPR. [FORBIDDEN: give_epinephrine_1mg_iv, give_amiodarone_300mg, give_lidocaine_alternative] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.4: Hypothermic Arrest; Brown DJA, NEJM 2012

recommendations.text: Tension pneumothorax is a reversible cause of PEA arrest; needle decompression is immediately life-saving. [REQUIRED: needle_decompression] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.2: Hs and Ts; Roberts DJ, Injury 2014

recommendations.text: Tension pneumothorax in arrest needs immediate needle decompression; waiting for imaging or medication-only approach is fatal. [FORBIDDEN: delay_needle_decompression_for_xray_in_arrest, give_only_epinephrine_in_tension_pneumo_arrest] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; tension pneumothorax in arrest requires immediate needle decompression; medications alone cannot resolve obstruction

recommendations.text: Routine bicarbonate in VF/pVT is not recommended; it delays defibrillation and may worsen intracellular acidosis via CO2 generation. [FORBIDDEN: give_routine_bicarbonate_in_shockable_arrest, delay_defibrillation_for_bicarbonate_push] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; routine sodium bicarbonate is not recommended in shockable arrest; it delays defibrillation and worsens intracellular acidosis

recommendations.text: Routine bicarbonate in PEA/asystole is not recommended and should not replace epinephrine as first-line treatment. [FORBIDDEN: give_routine_bicarbonate_in_nonshockable_arrest, substitute_bicarbonate_for_epinephrine_in_pea] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; routine bicarbonate not indicated in PEA/asystole

recommendations.text: For asystole/PEA, epinephrine should be given as soon as feasible. Atropine is no longer recommended for asystole (removed 2010). Focus on identifying and treating reversible causes.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Non-Shockable Rhythm Pathway (Asystole/PEA), the following actions are mandatory: - continue high quality cpr - give epinephrine 1mg iv immediately (within 3 minutes) - evaluate reversible causes (within 10 minutes)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Non-Shockable Rhythm Pathway (Asystole/PEA), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay cpr.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: atropine no longer recommended for asystole/PEA; removed from ACLS algorithm in 2010 due to lack of evidence [FORBIDDEN: give_atropine_for_asystole] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 5.2; atropine removed from asystole/PEA algorithm in 2010

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: defibrillation is only for shockable rhythms (VF/pVT); delivering shock in asystole delays CPR without benefit [FORBIDDEN: deliver_defibrillation_asystole] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 5.2; defibrillation has no role in asystole

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: amiodarone is indicated only for refractory VF/pVT; no role in asystole or PEA [FORBIDDEN: give_amiodarone_for_asystole] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 5.2; amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic for refractory VF/pVT only

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: routine bicarbonate not recommended unless severe acidosis (pH <7.1) or known hyperkalemia [FORBIDDEN: give_sodium_bicarbonate_routine] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 6.2; bicarbonate only for severe acidosis (pH <7.1) or hyperkalemia

recommendations.text: In non-shockable rhythms, epinephrine is given immediately (not delayed until after 2nd cycle as in shockable rhythms). [REQUIRED: give_epinephrine_1mg_iv_immediately] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 5.2; Perkins GD, NEJM 2018 (PARAMEDIC2)

recommendations.text: Cardiac tamponade is a reversible cause of PEA arrest; pericardiocentesis is life-saving. [REQUIRED: pericardiocentesis] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.2: Hs and Ts; Budhram GR, Acad Emerg Med 2019

recommendations.text: Cardiac tamponade in arrest needs immediate pericardiocentesis; vasopressors without drainage cannot restore circulation. [FORBIDDEN: delay_pericardiocentesis_for_imaging_in_arrest, give_vasopressors_only_in_tamponade_arrest] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; cardiac tamponade in arrest requires immediate pericardiocentesis; vasopressors alone cannot overcome obstruction

recommendations.text: For suspected opioid-related cardiac arrest, naloxone should be administered alongside standard ACLS. [REQUIRED: give_naloxone] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.5: Opioid-Related Arrest; Panchal AR, Circulation 2020

recommendations.text: Additional opioids or sedatives during opioid-associated cardiac arrest worsen respiratory and cardiac depression. [FORBIDDEN: give_additional_opioid_during_arrest, give_long_acting_sedative_during_arrest] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; additional CNS depressants worsen arrest prognosis

recommendations.text: In pregnant patients >20 weeks, perimortem cesarean delivery should begin within 4 minutes if no ROSC; left uterine displacement improves venous return. [REQUIRED: prepare_perimortem_cesarean, perform_left_uterine_displacement] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA 2025 Section 6.6: Cardiac Arrest in Pregnancy; Jeejeebhoy FM, Circulation 2015

recommendations.text: Perimortem C-section must begin within 4 minutes of maternal arrest; supine positioning compresses IVC reducing CPR blood flow. [FORBIDDEN: delay_perimortem_csection_beyond_4min, place_pregnant_arrest_patient_supine] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2020; perimortem C-section within 4 min of arrest; aortocaval compression reduces CPR efficacy

recommendations.text: During CPR, systematically consider and treat the Hs and Ts: Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Hydrogen ion (acidosis), Hypo-/hyperkalemia, Hypothermia, Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins, Thrombosis (PE or MI).
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Reversible Causes (Hs and Ts), the following actions are mandatory: - evaluate reversible causes (within 10 minutes)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Reversible Causes (Hs and Ts), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay cpr, terminate resuscitation prematurely.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: Targeted temperature management between 32-36C for at least 24 hours is recommended. Neuroprognostication should not be performed before 72 hours after ROSC.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: For Post-Cardiac Arrest Care, the following actions are mandatory: - initiate targeted temperature management (within 60 minutes) - obtain 12 lead ecg (within 60 minutes) - optimize hemodynamics (within 15 minutes) - admit to icu
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: During Post-Cardiac Arrest Care, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge home, terminate care prematurely.
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: neuroprognostication before 72h after ROSC is unreliable due to effects of sedation, hypothermia, and early brain injury evolution [FORBIDDEN: neuroprognosticate_before_72h] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA ACLS 2025 Section 7; Sandroni C, Intensive Care Med 2014

key_sections.overview: Advanced cardiac life support algorithm for adult cardiac arrest management Key evidence: High-quality CPR with minimal interruptions and early defibrillation for VF/pVT improve survival to discharge (Kudenchuk PJ, NEJM 2016)
key_sections.cardiac_arrest_initial_assessment: Confirm cardiac arrest, activate code team, begin high-quality CPR immediately Guideline states: High-quality CPR with a compression rate of 100-120/min, depth of 5-6 cm, full recoil, and minimal interruptions is the foundation of resuscitation. Required actions: confirm_cardiac_arrest, activate_code_team, begin_high_quality_cpr, attach_defibrillator_pads Contraindicated: delay_cpr, delay_defibrillation, interrupt_cpr_for_intubation_extended
key_sections.rhythm_assessment: Assess cardiac rhythm to determine shockable vs non-shockable pathway Guideline states: After initial CPR, check rhythm. If VF/pVT, proceed to defibrillation. If asystole/PEA, continue CPR and administer epinephrine. Required actions: analyze_rhythm Contraindicated: delay_cpr, interrupt_cpr_prolonged

Epinephrine should be given after the second shock. Amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered for shock-refractory VF/pVT. In shockable rhythm, defibrillation takes absolute priority; amiodarone before first shock and intubation delays worsen outcomes. Hyperkalemia is a reversible cause of cardiac arrest; calcium chloride stabilizes myocardium, bicarbonate and insulin shift potassium intracellularly. Succinylcholine worsens hyperkalemia via K+ release from muscle; calcium gluconate delay prolongs fatal cardiac toxicity. Below 30C, cardiac drugs are ineffective and may accumulate to toxic levels; focus on rewarming and CPR. Tension pneumothorax is a reversible cause of PEA arrest; needle decompression is immediately life-saving. Tension pneumothorax in arrest needs immediate needle decompression; waiting for imaging or medication-only approach is fatal. Routine bicarbonate in PEA/asystole is not recommended and should not replace epinephrine as first-line treatment.

key_sections.reversible_causes_(hs_and_ts): Systematic evaluation of reversible causes: Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Hydrogen ion, Hypo/hyperkalemia, Hypothermia, Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins, Thrombosis (pulmonary/coronary) Guideline states: During CPR, systematically consider and treat the Hs and Ts: Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Hydrogen ion (acidosis), Hypo-/hyperkalemia, Hypothermia, Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins, Thrombosis (PE or MI). Required actions: evaluate_reversible_causes Contraindicated: delay_cpr, terminate_resuscitation_prematurely
